thread.title: Apple’s (AAPL) “Buy” Rating Reaffirmed at Morgan Stanley

author: Sebastian Weber
title: Apple’s (AAPL) “Buy” Rating Reaffirmed at Morgan Stanley
text:
Posted by Sebastian Weber on Feb 15th, 2018 // No Comments 
Morgan Stanley restated their buy rating on shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) in a research report report published on Tuesday, January 23rd. Morgan Stanley currently has a $205.00 price target on the iPhone maker’s stock, up from their previous price target of $200.00. 
A number of other research firms have also commented on AAPL. Mizuho set a $160.00 price objective on Apple and gave the stock a hold rating in a research note on Wednesday, October 18th. Vetr lowered Apple from a buy rating to a hold rating and set a $178.34 price objective on the stock. in a research note on Friday, December 1st. UBS Group set a $190.00 price objective on Apple and gave the stock a buy rating in a research note on Friday, January 5th. Needham & Company LLC raised their price objective on Apple from $175.00 to $200.00 and gave the stock a buy rating in a research note on Friday, November 3rd. Finally, Instinet lowered Apple from a buy rating to a neutral rating and set a $175.00 price objective on the stock. in a research note on Tuesday, December 19th. Two analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, sixteen have given a hold rating, thirty-three have given a buy rating and two have assigned a strong buy rating to the company. The stock currently has an average rating of Buy and an average target price of $201.72. Get Apple alerts: 
Shares of Apple ( NASDAQ:AAPL ) traded up $3.03 during midday trading on Tuesday, hitting $167.37. The stock had a trading volume of 40,640,000 shares, compared to its average volume of 40,150,000. The company has a market capitalization of $849,240.00, a price-to-earnings ratio of 16.38, a P/E/G ratio of 1.23 and a beta of 1.33. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74, a quick ratio of 1.20 and a current ratio of 1.24. Apple has a one year low of $133.25 and a one year high of $180.10. 
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last announced its earnings results on Thursday, February 1st. The iPhone maker reported $3.89 earnings per share for the quarter, topping the Zacks’ consensus estimate of $3.82 by $0.07. The company had revenue of $88.29 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $87.62 billion. Apple had a return on equity of 37.37% and a net margin of 21.13%. The firm’s quarterly revenue was up 12.7% compared to the same quarter last year. During the same quarter last year, the company earned $3.36 earnings per share. research analysts predict that Apple will post 11.4 earnings per share for the current fiscal year. 
The company also recently announced a quarterly dividend, which will be paid on Thursday, February 15th. Investors of record on Monday, February 12th will be given a $0.63 dividend. This represents a $2.52 dividend on an annualized basis and a yield of 1.51%. The ex-dividend date of this dividend is Friday, February 9th. Apple’s payout ratio is 24.66%. 
In related news, insider Daniel J. Riccio sold 15,641 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction dated Friday, January 5th. The stock was sold at an average price of $174.78, for a total value of $2,733,733.98. Following the completion of the sale, the insider now directly owns 13,739 shares of the company’s stock, valued at approximately $2,401,302.42. The sale was disclosed in a filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is accessible through this link . Also, insider Johny Srouji sold 10,368 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction dated Friday, November 24th. The shares were sold at an average price of $174.68, for a total value of $1,811,082.24. Following the completion of the sale, the insider now directly owns 81,560 shares of the company’s stock, valued at $14,246,900.80. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Insiders sold a total of 112,771 shares of company stock valued at $19,419,429 over the last ninety days. 0.06% of the stock is currently owned by corporate insiders. 
Institutional investors have recently modified their holdings of the stock. Janus Henderson Group PLC boosted its stake in shares of Apple by 301.3% in the 2nd quarter. Janus Henderson Group PLC now owns 20,003,587 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $2,880,992,000 after buying an additional 15,018,790 shares during the last quarter. Harbour Capital Advisors LLC now owns 4,515,315 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $31,352,000 after buying an additional 4,483,360 shares during the last quarter. Amundi Pioneer Asset Management Inc. now owns 13,228,306 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $2,238,624,000 after buying an additional 4,448,509 shares during the last quarter. Truepoint Inc. boosted its stake in shares of Apple by 15,559.4% in the 3rd quarter. Truepoint Inc. now owns 4,436,774 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $4,437,000 after buying an additional 4,408,441 shares during the last quarter. Finally, Capital Research Global Investors boosted its stake in shares of Apple by 15.0% in the 2nd quarter. Capital Research Global Investors now owns 29,449,961 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $4,241,383,000 after buying an additional 3,845,363 shares during the last quarter. 60.18% of the stock is owned by institutional investors and hedge funds. Apple Company Profile 
Apple Inc (Apple) designs, manufactures and markets mobile communication and media devices, personal computers, and portable digital music players, and a variety of related software, services, peripherals, networking solutions, and third-party digital content and applications. The Company’s products and services include iPhone, iPad, Mac, iPod, Apple TV, a portfolio of consumer and professional software applications, the iOS and OS X operating systems, iCloud, and a variety of accessory, service and support offerings.
